the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.player: What's all this about?

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Martin Holt
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: Ah, hello and welcome. I'm Martin Holt, leader of Kourend's Royal Society. This is our little protest against the Kourend Council.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.player: Pleased to meet you, I'm [player name]. So, what's wrong with the Council?

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Martin Holt
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: Now there's a question! I have a better one. What's right with the Council?

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Martin Holt
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: I bet you didn't know that the Council was originally only temporary. After the last King died, they were only supposed to rule until his daughter came of age.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Martin Holt
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: However, according to the Council, the King's daughter went mad. Such a wonderful convenience for them of course. With her out of the picture, the Council became permanent.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.player: Interesting. What else don't you like about the Council?

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Martin Holt
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: Democracy! That's meant to be the big thing for the Council. Funny thing is, although they're meant to be elected by the people, the same four people have won every single election. Little odd, no?

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.player: That is a bit suspicious, I suppose.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: If the player doesn't have the requirements to start A Kingdom Divided.

steps.speaker: Martin Holt
steps.text: Indeed it is. So, do you want to join our protest?

steps.player: Not right now. But thanks for the information.

steps.text: You do not meet all of the requirements to start the A Kingdom Divided quest.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: If the player has the requirements to start A Kingdom Divided.

steps.speaker: Martin Holt
steps.text: Oh my friend, suspicious is the dish of the day whenever the Council is around. And what I've just told you barely scratches the surface. Things have been getting even worse recently.

options.text: Yes.

steps.player: How so?

steps.speaker: Martin Holt
steps.text: Do you know of Councillor Sophia Hughes? Lovely lady. Spends her free time with the Disciples of Yama, a wonderful cult of Zamorakian demon summoners.

steps.player: Councillor Hughes? I was the one who helped imprison her in the first place.

steps.speaker: Martin Holt
steps.text: Ah, so you're the adventurer who's been cooking up a storm around here. Well you'll be pleased to know your hard work was all for nothing. Councillor Hughes has escaped. Lucky her.

steps.player: Escaped? How?

steps.speaker: Martin Holt
steps.text: Believe it or not, no one actually knows. The Council is trying to keep it all on the down low of course. Almost like they have something to hide.

steps.player: That's quite the accusation. Do you have proof?

steps.speaker: Martin Holt
steps.text: Oh, we will soon! Just you give it time. They'll slip up sooner or later.

steps.player: Hmm... Rather than just waiting for that to happen, maybe I could investigate her escape.

steps.speaker: Martin Holt
steps.text: What an interesting idea. I suppose you would be well placed to have a little nosey, considering your history with the Councillor. Though you'd need to get permission, of course.

steps.player: How would I do that?

steps.speaker: Martin Holt
steps.text: I hear the Kourend Royal Guard are leading the investigation. Commander Lydia Fullore is their leader. You'll find her in the castle.

steps.player: I'll go speak to her.

steps.speaker: Martin Holt
steps.text: Good luck friend. Your eyes are open now. Don't trust the Council.

options.text: No.

steps.player: Well, I think I'll stay out of this one. Good luck with your protest.

steps.speaker: Martin Holt
steps.text: As you wish, but you shouldn't be afraid to open your eyes. If you change your mind, we'll be here.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.player: Hey there. Remind me, where can I find Commander Fullore?

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Martin Holt
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: She'll be somewhere in the castle.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.player: Thank you.
Hello. Who are you?

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: I'm Commander Lydia Fullore, leader of the Kourend Royal Guard.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.player: Then you're just the person I'm looking for. I'm [player name]. I hear you're the one to talk to about the recent escape of Councillor Hughes.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: Ah, let me guess, you've been talking to Martin Holt?

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.player: You know him?

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: Oh, I know him alright. Martin and I have quite the history.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.player: Really? He didn't mention it.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: He wouldn't. He has a very selective memory. I imagine he also didn't mention that he used to work for the Council that he hates so much.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.player: No... that's not something that ever came up.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: Well I imagine his Royal Society friends wouldn't make so much of him if they knew where his loyalties used to lie.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.player: So I'm guessing you don't agree with his views on the Council.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: Well I wouldn't be very good at my job if I did. Martin is always quick to point out the failings of the Council, but he conveniently forgets about all the good they've done.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.player: Like?

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: You know that smell in Port Piscarilius?

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.player: It is a bit ripe there.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: Imagine that but ten times worse. That's what it was like before the Council had a new sewage system installed. The entire kingdom is now cleaner and safer because of them.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: Not only that, but without the Council, you wouldn't even be stood here. It was under them that trade with your lands to the east was established.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: Without those trade routes, you would have no easy way of getting here.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: I could go on, but I have more urgent things to attend to.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.player: Like the escape of Councillor Hughes?

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: Well, since it's clearly no secret, yes. The former Councillor is a dangerous individual, so I want her back in a cell as soon as possible.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.player: You know, I might be able to help you with that. In case you didn't know, I was the one who helped catch her in the first place.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: So, this is what Martin has put you up to! Well, no thank you. The last thing I need is one of his people getting in the way.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.player: I'm not one of his people! I barely know him. I'm just a willing adventurer who wants to help.

Think about it. However this investigation goes, you'll be seen as biased towards the Council. I'm a neutral third party with no ties to the Councillor or the protesters. I'm in an ideal position to help out here.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: Hmm... you do have the experience. And I can't deny, the fact that you have the support of the protesters could be useful.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: This whole situation with Councillor Hughes has caused enough civil unrest. We certainly don't need it to get any worse.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: Alright, you can help. But for the duration of this investigation, you're working for me. What I say goes, is that clear?

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.player: Crystal clear. Where do we start?

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: Right now we don't have any leads on where Councillor Hughes might have gone. I'm heading over to her home to see if there's anything there that can help us. You should join me.

options.text: Let's get going.

steps.player: Let's get going.

steps.text: A cutscene begins. The player and Commander Fullore approach Kingstown, and are stopped by Tomas Lawry and Captain Ginea.

steps.speaker: Tomas Lawry
steps.text: Commander Fullore! How wonderful to see you.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Tomas! What are you doing here?

steps.speaker: Tomas Lawry
steps.text: Why, I'm here about Sophia Hughes of course! As the person who discovered her corruption in the first place, I was an obvious choice to lead the investigation into her disappearance.

steps.player: But that wasn't you! I did all the work!

steps.speaker: Tomas Lawry
steps.text: Ah, and hello again, my financially challenged friend! Of course, the capture of Sophia Hughes wouldn't have been possible without your minor contributions.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: The Kourend Royal Guard are conducting the investigation, Tomas. Your presence is not needed.

steps.speaker: Tomas Lawry
steps.text: Well, that's just the thing. Councillor Andrews was so impressed with my work, he put me in charge of this investigation.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: That is not his call to make! I'm in charge of Council security. This investigation is mine to lead!

steps.speaker: Tomas Lawry
steps.text: He is head of the Council. If he wants to make that call, he can.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Regardless...

steps.speaker: Tomas Lawry
steps.text: Look, I can see you're very passionate, which is wonderful. Tell you what, as you're so eager, I'll allow you both to help me in my investigation.

steps.speaker: Tomas Lawry
steps.text: Do join me inside when you're ready.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Captain Ginea. I'm guessing Lord Shayzien sent you.

steps.speaker: Captain Ginea
steps.text: He did. He's keen to see this Hughes business sorted quickly.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: He's not alone there, but he doesn't need to worry. We have things under control.

steps.speaker: Captain Ginea
steps.text: Forgive me Commander, but it doesn't seem like you do. Hughes escaped from right under your nose, and now Councillor Andrews is putting his faith in Lawry over you.

steps.speaker: Captain Ginea
steps.text: While this may be Council business, Lord Shayzien is responsible for dealing with both internal and external threats. He wants to be sure that Hughes won't be an issue.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: You have my word. She'll be back in a cell before the day is out.

steps.speaker: Captain Ginea
steps.text: I hope you're right. There's already a lot of doubt in the Council these days. It would be rather embarrassing for them if the Shayzien Army had to step in.

steps.player: For someone who supports the Council so much, you don't seem very happy about Councillor Andrews' decision.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: I can support the Council while not agreeing with every choice they make.

steps.player: I feel like you're not totally being honest with me.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Would that be so wrong? I hardly know you.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Here's some advice for you: focus on the investigation. Leave the politics to the experts.

steps.player: Fine. I guess we'd better get started.

steps.text: Cutscene ends, and the player is now in front of Councillor Hughes' house.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Have a look around the house and see if you can find any hints on where Councillor Hughes might have gone. I'll ask around out here and see if anyone's seen anything suspicious.

steps.player: Sounds good.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Good luck. Don't let Lawry get in your way.

options.text: I just need to do something first.

steps.player: I just need to do something first.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Okay, just let me know when you're ready to depart.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: Are you ready to head over to Councillor Hughes' home?

options.text: Let's get going.
I just need to do something first.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Martin Holt
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: Hello again. I hope things are going well.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.player: Not too bad thanks.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Martin Holt
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: Well, keep up the good work. After all, it would be very awkward for our friends on the Council if you caught Sophia Hughes again.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Tomas Lawry
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: Hello again. Your desire to help out with my investigation is to be commended, but you really shouldn't worry. I'll have the former Councillor back in a cell in no time.

options.text: So you already have some leads?

steps.player: So you already have some leads?

steps.speaker: Tomas Lawry
steps.text: Not just yet. It won't be long though. Not with my resourcefulness!

steps.player: Yeah... second only to your humility.

steps.speaker: Tomas Lawry
steps.text: How very kind of you. I should tell you though, a skillset like mine isn't gained over night. If you wish to become like me, it will take a lot of hard work.

steps.player: I'll keep that in mind. Anyway, I should get back to work.

options.text: I've found something that might be useful.

steps.player: I've found something that might be useful.

steps.speaker: Tomas Lawry
steps.text: Oh yes? What is it?

steps.player: Looks like the Councillor might be hiding out at Mount Quidamortem.

steps.speaker: Tomas Lawry
steps.text: Mount Quidamortem? That's quite the trek.

steps.player: I could go if you like?

steps.speaker: Tomas Lawry
steps.text: How very kind of you, but no need. This is my investigation, and I will handle it.
Tomas departs for Mount Quidamortem.

steps.player: Sucker.

options.text: If you say so.

steps.player: If you say so.

options.text: I think I know where Councillor Hughes has gone.

steps.player: I think I know where Councillor Hughes has gone.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Where?

options.text: The Farming Guild.

steps.player: The Farming Guild.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Huh, not where I'd have expected. But maybe that's the point.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: If you think that's where she is, I'd recommend you go and check it out. I'll keep an eye on things here.

steps.player: Okay. Where abouts is it?

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: North of the River Molch, west of here.

steps.player: Thanks.

options.text: The Deeper Lode.

steps.player: The Deeper Lode.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Seems a risky place for her to go. I'd have thought she'd pick somewhere quieter.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: If you're sure though, I'd recommend you go and scout it out. I'll keep an eye on things here.

steps.player: Okay. Where abouts is it?

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: It's the pub in Lovakengj, north west of here.

steps.player: Thanks.

options.text: The Little Shop of Horace.

steps.player: The Little Shop of Horace.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: You don't think Horace is helping her, do you?

steps.player: Well we can't make any assumptions.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: True. If that's where you think she is, I suggest you go and check it out. I'll keep an eye on things here.

steps.player: Okay. Where abouts is it?

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: It's the general store in Hosidius, south east of here.

steps.player: Thanks.

options.text: The Chasm of Fire.

steps.player: The Chasm of Fire.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: That's where most of her cultist friends spend their time, seems a bit obvious.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: I guess it could still be worth a look. If you think she's there, you should go and scout it out. I'll keep an eye on things here.

steps.player: Okay. Where abouts is it?

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: On the outskirts of Shayzien, west of here.

steps.player: Thanks.

options.text: Actually, I don't know.

steps.player: Actually, I don't know.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Well, keep looking around. There must be something here that can help us.

options.text: What was the date when Councillor Hughes escaped?

steps.player: What was the date when Councillor Hughes escaped?

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: It was two days ago, on the 26th of Fentuary.

steps.player: Hang on... If she escaped two days ago, why are we only searching her house now?

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: The start of the investigation was... delayed. I can't say any more.

steps.player: Hmm...

options.text: Did you know there's a demon upstairs?

steps.player: Did you know there's a demon upstairs?

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: A demon? Well I guess the Disciples of Yama are known for that sort of thing. Still, that's going to be a nightmare to deal with. Can it get out?

steps.player: I don't think so.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Good. Do your best to avoid it and we'll worry about it later.

options.text: What should I be doing?

steps.player: What should I be doing?

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Have a look around the house and see if you can find any hints on where Councillor Hughes might have gone. I'll ask around out here and see if anyone's noticed anything suspicious.

steps.player: Sounds good. I'll let you know if I find anything.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.player: Hello. I'm looking for Sophia Hughes.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Sergeant
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: Sophia Hughes? The councillor?

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.player: That's right. I think she might have come here at some point.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Sergeant
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: Well, if she did it wasn't recently. We'd have noticed a councillor.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.player: I see. Thanks for the help.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Horace
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: Hello, I'm Horace. Welcome to my shop. Would you like to buy or sell something?

options.text: Who are you?
Okay, let's trade.
Had any councillors shop here recently?

steps.player: Had any councillors shop here recently?

steps.speaker: Horace
steps.text: Not as far as I can recall. Councillor Hughes used to order things from time to time, before she was arrested. None of the others have ever shopped here though.

steps.player: Hmm, fair enough.

options.text: No, I'm fine.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Disciple of Yama
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: Welcome. Have you come to give your soul to the Chasm?

options.text: Uh, I believe I'm still using it.
I'm looking for Sophia Hughes.

steps.player: I'm looking for Sophia Hughes.

steps.speaker: Disciple of Yama
steps.text: You are not alone in that, but you will not find her here.

steps.player: She's one of your lot though, right? This seems like a good place for her to hide.

steps.speaker: Disciple of Yama
steps.text: You are welcome to go in and check. You will find nothing. Sophia Hughes no longer has a place here.

steps.player: Hmm, if you say so.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Fuggy
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: Hello, human. What's your pleasure today?

options.text: Let's see what you've got.
I don't want to talk about my pleasure.
Had any councillors stay here recently?

steps.player: Had any councillors stay here recently?

steps.speaker: Fuggy
steps.text: Councillors? What do you mean?

steps.player: I'm investigating the disappearance of Councillor Sophia Hughes. I have reason to believe she rented a bed here.

steps.speaker: Fuggy
steps.text: A disappearing councillor? That's a new one. We don't really get many humans renting beds here. The only one recently was a woman who stayed here last night, but she didn't look much like a councillor.

steps.player: She could have been in disguise. Do you know where this woman is now?

steps.speaker: Fuggy
steps.text: Well she left not long before you got here. I didn't really speak to her but I did hear her mention something about catching a ship at Port Piscarilius.

steps.player: A ship? She's trying to escape! Do you know which ship?

steps.speaker: Fuggy
steps.text: Well let's see now...
The ground shakes.

steps.speaker: Fuggy
steps.text: Blimy! That was a good one!

steps.player: What on Gielinor was that?

steps.speaker: Fuggy
steps.text: Ah, not from around here are you? That was an earthquake. We get them here from time to time. I think they come from that volcano to the west, but I'm no expert.

steps.speaker: Fuggy
steps.text: Anyway, what were we on about?

steps.player: The Councillor.

steps.speaker: Fuggy
steps.text: Ah yes, the Councillor. I seem to recall her mentioning Veos. It must be his ship she's taking.

steps.player: I need to get there quick. Thank you for the help.

steps.speaker: Fuggy
steps.text: Not a problem. Good luck with your search.

options.text: Have you heard any rumours here?
I'm alright, thank you.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Fuggy
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: Hello, human. What's your pleasure today?

options.text: Let's see what you've got.
I don't want to talk about my pleasure.
So about the Councillor.

steps.player: So about the Councillor.

steps.speaker: Fuggy
steps.text: You again? I've already told you everything. The woman mentioned Veos over at Port Piscarilius. She must be catching his ship.

steps.player: Ah yes. I need to get there quickly.

steps.speaker: Fuggy
steps.text: Fuggy: Good luck.

options.text: Have you heard any rumours here?
I'm alright, thank you.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.player: Err, where's Veos?

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Cabin Boy Herbert
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: Your guess is as good as mine. He was here until that earthquake. Then he suddenly just wandered off, like he was in some sort of trance.

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.player: But what about his ship?

the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.speaker: Cabin Boy Herbert
the-disgraced-councillor-s-escape-talkin.text: I guess I'll have to look after it until he comes back. I hope he won't be long. I'm not really cut out for this kind of thing.

options.text: Can you take me somewhere?
I'm looking for a councillor.

steps.player: I'm looking for a councillor.

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Herbert
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.player: I believe Councillor Sophia Hughes is planning to board this ship. I need to find her.

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Herbert
steps.text: The one that got arrested? If she wants to board the ship she'll need to do it soon. We're nearly ready to cast off. I guess you could wait around and see if she shows up.

steps.player: Not a bad idea. I think I'll do just that.

steps.text: A cutscene begins. Commander Fullore arrives at the port.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Heard you were out here. Thought I'd come see how things are going.

steps.player: Not spying on me are you?

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Spying is a strong word. I just like to keep an eye on people I've not worked with before. Especially in a situation as delicate as this one.

steps.player: That's one way of putting it.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: So, what of Hughes?

steps.player: She booked passage on this ship, but she's not arrived yet. If she's coming, it will be soon.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: And we'll be here when she does. Not bad.

steps.player: Starting to trust me now?

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Don't get ahead of yourself.

steps.player: Ah, looks like we might have a visitor.

steps.text: Sophia Hughes arrives at the port. The music track Confrontation plays.

steps.player: Sophia Hughes. Going somewhere?

steps.speaker: Sophia Hughes
steps.text: You! This is all your doing!

steps.player: The only person to blame is yourself. When you play with fire, you get burnt.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: It's over, Sophia. You should come quietly.

steps.speaker: Sophia Hughes
steps.text: Commander Fullore! He would send you, wouldn't he? The little lapdog of Councillor Andrews!

steps.speaker: Sophia Hughes
steps.text: He knew, you know! They all did. They were more than happy with my work while it was secret. But now they betray me without a second thought, just to protect themselves!

steps.speaker: Sophia Hughes
steps.text: You'd think they'd have some loyalty after all we did! After what we did to him. After what we did to his girl! We were in it together until it no longer suited them!

steps.player: What are you on about? What girl?

steps.speaker: Sophia Hughes
steps.text: Don't think I'm coming quietly! I've fought too hard to stop now!

steps.speaker: Sophia Hughes
steps.text: Judge of Yama, hear my voice! I call upon you to bring justice to the unworthy! Cleanse them in a sea of fire! Cleanse them in a sea of blood!
Sophia Hughes casts a spell.

steps.speaker: Demonic Voice
steps.text: Sophia Hughes. You have called upon me. Those that oppose you will be judged in the name of Yama.

steps.speaker: Demonic Voice
steps.text: But know this, Sophia Hughes. Those that call upon the Judge must first be judged themselves.

steps.speaker: Demonic Voice
steps.text: You have betrayed the trust of Yama, Sophia Hughes. You have used his generosity to your own advantage. For this, your life is forfeit.

steps.speaker: Sophia Hughes
steps.text: What? No!

steps.speaker: Demonic Voice
steps.text: Come. Serve your master one last time. Bathe yourself in a sea of fire. Bathe yourself in a sea of blood.

steps.speaker: Sophia Hughes
steps.text: No... Wait!
Sophia Hughes is burnt to a crisp, and in her place the Judge of Yama appears before the player and Commander Fullore.

steps.speaker: Judge of Yama
steps.text: And so the justice of Yama has been brought upon Sophia Hughes, as it will be brought upon all who wrong him.

steps.speaker: Judge of Yama
steps.text: Lydia Fullore, [player name]. You have been declared enemies of Yama. Your actions have endangered the work of his children. For this, your lives are forfeit.

steps.player: Hey! You can't just show up and start incinerating people. That's not how justice works. How about you clear off, before I make you!

steps.speaker: Judge of Yama
steps.text: [player name]. You have challenged the Judge of Yama. Your guilt will be determined through combat.

steps.speaker: Judge of Yama
steps.text: Should you succeed, you will be free of your sins. Should you fail, you will be bathed in fire. You will be bathed in blood.

steps.speaker: Judge of Yama
steps.text: Now, in the name of Yama, let us begin.

options.text: Well, good luck.

kourend-s-last-princess-meeting-with-cou.speaker: Councillor Andrews
kourend-s-last-princess-meeting-with-cou.text: Here he is, the hero of the hour. On behalf of the Council, and indeed all of Kourend, thank you for dealing with this messy situation.

kourend-s-last-princess-meeting-with-cou.speaker: Councillor Andrews
kourend-s-last-princess-meeting-with-cou.text: You're far too humble. You've done so much for our kingdom in your short time here. Rest assured, we have noticed. In fact, I consider you a firm friend of the Council.

kourend-s-last-princess-meeting-with-cou.player: Have you managed to work out how Councillor Hughes escaped?

kourend-s-last-princess-meeting-with-cou.speaker: Councillor Andrews
kourend-s-last-princess-meeting-with-cou.text: Not yet. You need not worry though, we'll get to the bottom of it. That said, I do have another ask of you... if you don't mind.

kourend-s-last-princess-meeting-with-cou.speaker: Councillor Andrews
kourend-s-last-princess-meeting-with-cou.text: Commander Fullore tells me you've had dealings with Martin Holt and his group.

kourend-s-last-princess-meeting-with-cou.player: I'm not sure about dealings, but we've met.

kourend-s-last-princess-meeting-with-cou.speaker: Councillor Andrews
kourend-s-last-princess-meeting-with-cou.text: Well regardless, your handling of the situation with Sophia Hughes seems to have had quite an impact on them.

kourend-s-last-princess-meeting-with-cou.player: Well, I am quite impactful. So, what is this ask?

kourend-s-last-princess-meeting-with-cou.speaker: Councillor Andrews
kourend-s-last-princess-meeting-with-cou.text: This recent situation has been most unfortunate. People are angry, I understand that. That said, Sophia Hughes has been dealt with. It's time for Martin Holt and his protestors to go home.

kourend-s-last-princess-meeting-with-cou.player: Ah, I see. You want me to convince them.

kourend-s-last-princess-meeting-with-cou.speaker: Councillor Andrews
kourend-s-last-princess-meeting-with-cou.text: It would be greatly appreciated. Civil unrest is of no benefit to anyone. We'd all be better off putting this behind us.

kourend-s-last-princess-meeting-with-cou.speaker: Councillor Andrews
kourend-s-last-princess-meeting-with-cou.text: Now, I must be off. Plenty of work to do. Good luck with Martin and his friends.

kourend-s-last-princess-meeting-with-cou.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-meeting-with-cou.text: We're looking into how Sophia Hughes might have escaped. I'll let you know if we find anything.

kourend-s-last-princess-meeting-with-cou.player: You know that's not what I mean.

kourend-s-last-princess-meeting-with-cou.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-meeting-with-cou.text: I'm not sure what you're on about. Now, I'm sorry, but I need to get to work.

kourend-s-last-princess-meeting-with-cou.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-meeting-with-cou.text: whispers* Meet me just south of the castle.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.text: Councillor Hughes was a deranged cultist.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.text: I don't know...

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.player: Do you not know? Or do you just not want to admit it? The man and the girl she spoke of. What did she mean?

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.text: Ever since King Kharedst IV died, there have been those who have questioned his death. People like Martin.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.text: It was all just wild speculation, though. The King was old, and he died of an illness. It happens all the time.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.player: The man Councillor Hughes mentioned. It could have been the King she was referring to.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.text: Maybe. Or maybe it was someone else.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.player: And the girl she mentioned? The King had a daughter.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.text: Rose. She was meant to take the throne after him, but she was too young. His advisors took over until she came of age.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.player: The Council. It never went that way though, did it? She never took the throne. Martin said they declared her mad.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.text: Grief can do a lot to someone. Rose and her father were very close.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.text: Listen to us! Are we really considering this? The Council rule Kourend. They have done so successfully for 20 years now.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.player: What happened to Rose in the end? Where did she go?

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.text: After what happened, public life was no place for her. The Council arranged for her to move away so she could escape all of that.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.text: I don't know...

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.text: Look, I'm the commander of the Kourend Royal Guard. My duty is to the Council.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.player: As commander of the 'Royal Guard' your duty is surely to royalty, not to some Council.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.text: What kind of person would I be if I betrayed them?

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.player: What kind of person would you be if you followed them blindly, even when all the evidence says not to?

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.text: I'm sorry, but I can't.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.text: I can't! But you can.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.text: Councillor Andrews may have been all nice to you, but he's furious with me. He's blamed me for what happened in Port Piscarilius. I have no hope of doing anything now without him knowing.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.text: But you, on the other hand... You're just some adventurer as far as they're concerned. They won't be keeping an eye on you.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.text: Rose. If she's still alive, then she's the key to the truth. You have to find her.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.text: I'm going to hate myself for this, but I know someone who could help.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.text: Martin. He's leader of Kourend's Royal Society. He knows more about the last royal family than anyone. If anyone can help you find Rose, it's him.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.text: Now, I need to get back inside, before someone finds out I'm missing.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.player: Thank you, Lydia. I know this can't be easy for you.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.text: I really need to go. Speak to Martin, and good luck.
Commander Fullore heads back into the castle.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-comma.text: No time to talk I'm afraid. Didn't Councillor Andrews want you to speak to Martin Holt about his protest?

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: Hello again, friend. Isn't it a wonderful day? Sophia Hughes has been dealt with and our wonderfully corrupt Council are out rowing without a paddle. Keep up the good work!

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: Good to see you, friend. Excellent work with Sophia Hughes!

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.player: Hello Martin. I see your protest is growing.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: Indeed it is, friend. Would you believe it that apparently some councillor went and summoned a demon in Port Piscarilius? That made a lot of people angry.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.player: It seems the guards have also taken interest.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: No doubt sent by the Council to keep an eye on us. We've got them scared now.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.player: Maybe they think things will get violent?

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: And yet they're the ones with the weapons. Interesting, huh?

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: Anyway, what can I do for you, friend?

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.player: There's something important we need to talk about.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: Something important? Is it about the Council?

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.player: It is.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: Well, what is it? If you have news on the Council, we must let the people know at once.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.player: This one needs to stay between you and me.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: The people have a right to know, my friend.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.player: They do. But if what I've discovered is true, we can't let the Council realise we know until we have definitive proof.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: I see. This sounds serious. What have you learnt?

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.player: When I confronted Sophia Hughes, she spoke of things the Council did to a man and his daughter.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: A man and his daughter? Surely this can't mean...

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.player: Kharedst IV. The last King of Great Kourend.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: I knew it! I knew the Council were involved in his death!

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.player: Like I said, we have no proof. The dying words of a cultist are not going to be enough to convince many. We need real proof.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: And this is why you came to me? You have a plan?

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.player: The King's daughter, Rose. If we can find her, we might be able to find out what happened.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: But my friend, no one knows where Rose is! Some don't even think she's alive any more. Sadly, most people have just forgotten her completely.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.player: But you haven't! You must have some idea of where they might have taken her.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: I'm afraid not. However, I wonder if Rose herself might be able to help.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.player: Err... What?

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: The Council didn't declare Rose mad right away. It wasn't until a few weeks after her father died that she was moved away.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.player: But how does that help us?

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: Rose was well known for being a good writer, even at her young age. She documented everything she did. She even wrote her father's memoirs for him.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: If something happened in those few weeks, maybe she wrote about it.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.player: Ah, I understand now. That does make sense.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: If the player has not used the secret page on Kharedst's memoirs:

steps.player: You know, I actually ended up acquiring her father's memoirs myself.

steps.speaker: Martin Holt
steps.text: You did? Interesting. The memoirs were auctioned off recently, along with a lot of other royal possessions.

steps.speaker: Martin Holt
steps.text: The auction was a request from the King before he died. He wanted the money to go towards helping the poor of Kourend.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: If the player has used the secret page on Kharedst's memoirs:

steps.player: You know, I actually ended up acquiring her father's memoirs myself. There was an interesting page hidden in the book. It suggested that something bad happened to whoever wrote it.

steps.speaker: Martin Holt
steps.text: And you're only mentioning this now? You had proof that something happened to Rose, and you did nothing with it?

steps.player: Well it wasn't really proof of anything. It gave no details on what actually happened, and no leads to follow. It wasn't even clear if Rose wrote it.

steps.speaker: Martin Holt
steps.text: Even still, something like that might have been worth bringing up.

steps.player: Well, now you know. I don't see how it helps us, though.

steps.speaker: Martin Holt
steps.text: The memoirs were auctioned off recently, along with a lot of other royal possessions. The auction was a request from the King before he died. He wanted the money to go towards helping the poor of Kourend.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.player: The King's been dead for years. How come the auction only happened recently?

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: For that you can thank our Council friends. They blocked it for years. They said Rose's things should not be included, as the original request only covered her father's possessions.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: I did wonder if they had more malicious motivations, and now you've confirmed it. They clearly didn't want anyone getting their hands on Rose's writings.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.player: Were there any other writings, apart from the memoirs?

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: Yes. Rose's personal diary. It went to the Library Historical Archive. I hear they have it on display there.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.player: So I need to go to the Archive and get that diary.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: The Archive isn't the Library. You can't just borrow things. I doubt they'll let you take it.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.player: To be honest, I wasn't actually planning on asking.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: A [man/woman] who knows what needs to be done. I respect that. Talk to Archeio in the Arceuus Library. He can take you to the Archive. Come back once you have the diary and we'll discuss our next steps.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.player: What do I need to be doing?

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: Rose's personal diary is on display in the Library Historical Archive. We need to aquire it. Talk to Archeio in the Arceuus Library. He can take you to the Archive.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-istor.speaker: Istoria
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-istor.text: Welcome to the Library Historical Archive.

options.text: What is this place?
What do you do here?
I have a question about Rose.

steps.player: I have a question about Rose.

steps.speaker: Istoria
steps.text: Rose? The princess?

steps.player: That's right.

steps.speaker: Istoria
steps.text: Ah, poor girl. Her tale is such a tragic one. What would you like to know?

steps.player: I heard her diary was on display here. I was wondering if I could read it.

steps.speaker: Istoria
steps.text: You are correct that we have her diary. It's in the display case on the eastern wall. That said, I'm afraid I can't let you read it.

steps.speaker: Istoria
steps.text: The diary is here to be preserved. However, we do not feel it appropriate to let people read the private thoughts of a young girl.

steps.player: I see. Fair enough.

steps.speaker: Istoria
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: How do I get out of here?
Goodbye.

kourend-s-last-princess-returning-to-mar.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-returning-to-mar.text: Good to see you, friend. Any luck with that diary?
You give Rose's diary to Martin.

kourend-s-last-princess-returning-to-mar.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-returning-to-mar.text: Good work. Now, let's see if this diary has anything for us...

kourend-s-last-princess-returning-to-mar.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-returning-to-mar.text: Hmm. Doesn't look to be anything obvious, but that's not suprising. Anything too in your face would have been found by the Council long ago.
If the player has used the secret page on Kharedst's memoirs:

steps.player: The hidden page from the King's memoirs was hidden inside the book cover.

steps.speaker: Martin Holt
steps.text: Let's see if the same trick has been used here.

kourend-s-last-princess-returning-to-mar.text: If the player has not used the secret page on Kharedst's memoirs:

steps.speaker: Martin Holt
steps.text: Let's try this...

kourend-s-last-princess-returning-to-mar.text: Martin cuts open the cover of the diary and a note falls out.

kourend-s-last-princess-returning-to-mar.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-returning-to-mar.text: And what do we have here?

kourend-s-last-princess-returning-to-mar.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-returning-to-mar.text: Very interesting. See what you make of this.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: Well?

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.player: It's a riddle.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: That it is. It seems to be describing a location. If we find that location, maybe we'll find something of use.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: We should split up. The Council could be watching us, and I don't want to make anything too obvious. Let's see who can solve this thing first.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.player: Alright. Good luck.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: We should split up and try to solve the riddle. I'll regroup with you at wherever it leads us.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.player: Alright. Good luck.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: Well here we are.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.player: You think this is definitely it?

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: Forthos was the seat of the Hosidius family before it was destroyed in the War of the Five Houses. 'A seat of power, lost in a war of pride.'

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: Anyway, looks like I won this one. What's my prize?

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.player: I don't think there is one.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: Pah, that's where you're wrong my friend. This could lead us to the ultimate prize. This could lead us to the truth behind the delightful Kourend Council.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.player: You really do hate them don't you? You know, Lydia told me you worked for them once.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: Is that a problem?

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.player: Just interesting. You went from working for them to being their biggest opponent. What changed?

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: I opened my eyes. When I worked for the Council, I was young and naive. But over time, I came to see the truth.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: The tipping point came a couple of years ago. I was helping to manage the treasury at the time. We had a big donation come in from a private businessman. Lovely chap.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: He was ever so noble. Something eating away at his conscience, no doubt. He wanted the money to go towards improved education in Port Piscarilius. He felt it would help with the crime levels there.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: That was of course a big no-go for the Council. Helping the people? No chance! Instead, they used only a small amount for that. They spent the rest on castle renovations.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: They claimed the increase in castle tourism would make more money in the long run. A load of tosh! I knew it was just for them.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: I walked out that same day. Soon after, I founded Kourend's Royal Society. We've been a bane for the Council ever since.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.player: Why not mention this before?

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: Wasn't really important. I'm sure Lydia didn't tell you everything about herself either. We were together once, you know. But she was ever loyal to the Council.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: In the end she decided I wasn't her type, and went off with that Captain Ginea instead. Of course, that didn't work out either. One day she'll stop blaming her problems on everyone else.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.player: Is this relevant?

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: Nope. And neither is my history with the Council. Now, let's crack on. Rose led us here for a reason. There must be something hidden nearby.

steps.player: What do you know about Rose?

steps.speaker: Martin Holt
steps.text: She was born to King Kharedst IV as his first and only child. Her mother died when she was very young, so her father mostly looked after her on his own. The two were very close.

steps.speaker: Martin Holt
steps.text: She was only 11 when her father died. Even at that age, she had already proven that she was smart, capable and caring. She'd have made a good queen, but the Council put a stop to that.

steps.player: She was 11 when the King died? How old would that make her now?
31? So wherever she is, she's spent most of her life there. If she's still alive of course.

steps.speaker: Martin Holt
steps.text: You'd hope that even the Council wouldn't go as far as to kill her, but that's probably wishful thinking. They're as evil as they come.

options.text: What happens when we find Rose?

steps.speaker: Martin Holt
steps.text: Hopefully she can give us the truth about her father's death.

steps.player: Okay, but say the Council are guilty? What happens then?

steps.text: Oh they're guilty my friend, make no mistake. We just need proof. Once we have it, we can use it to have them removed from power.

steps.speaker: Martin Holt
steps.text: After that, Rose can take her rightful place on the throne.

steps.player: And if she's incapable of doing that?

steps.speaker: Martin Holt
steps.text: Let's cross that bridge if we get to it.

options.text: Tell me about Kourend's Royal Society.

steps.player: Tell me about Kourend's Royal Society.

steps.speaker: Martin Holt
steps.text: The throne of Kourend has sat empty for far too long. After all, what is a kingdom without a king? That was the question I asked myself when I created the society.

steps.speaker: Martin Holt
steps.text: You see, I'd grown tired of our wonderful Council and their dishonourable ways. I wanted a return to how things used to be. Turns out I wasn't alone.

steps.speaker: Martin Holt
steps.text: Kourend's Royal Society offers a place for likeminded individuals to share and debate their views without fear of being judged.

steps.player: It's not just about debate though is it? You're trying to spread your views to others with your protests.

steps.speaker: Martin Holt
steps.text: We know the Council to be corrupt. We feel it only right that all of Kourend know that. The people have a right to the truth.

steps.player: It's interesting that you focus on power for the people but desire a monarchy. Surely a democracy would be more fitting?

steps.speaker: Martin Holt
steps.text: Democracy is just a façade, my friend. The Council! They're meant to be a democracy! It's all a load of rubbish. Democracy is just a way of pretending the people have power.

steps.player: Maybe, but I don't see how you fix that with a king or queen.

steps.speaker: Martin Holt
steps.text: Kings and queens are raised from birth to rule. They know how to do it right. Under a king or queen, this kingdom would flourish.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.player: Even so, I wonder how she set it all up?

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: Never underestimate a child, my friend. I remember a gang of thieves a few years back that used them heavily. The kids could get places the adults couldn't. No one ever suspected them either.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.text: They were such a problem that the Council had to get Lord Shayzien to send some soldiers in to deal with them. Lydia was one of them. This was before she joined the Royal Guard.

kourend-s-last-princess-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: What of the Councillor? Where is he?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: The player opens the cell gates.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: You can come out now.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: Councillor.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: Commander.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: Liam... tell me it isn't true.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: I'm sorry Lydia.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: I defended you! I defended all of you! And all this time, you've been lying!

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: I swear to you, we did it for the people.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: Don't give me that!

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: Look at her! Look at what you did to her! She was a child, Liam!

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: I'm sorry.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: What did you do to her? Why is she like this?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: We didn't want to kill her. She didn't deserve that. The mage gave us a potion. He said it would stop her revealing the truth.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: Mage? What mage?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: There was an Arceuus mage. He was an expert in curses, and he realised what was happening. He gave us the poison for the King.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: Would have been nice for you to mention this earlier! Who was this mage?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: He never told us his name.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: And you trusted him? Are you serious? Some random mage comes along and tells you to poison the King and you just... do it?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: Everything the mage said was true. The King was cursed. We could see it.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: Did it ever cross your mind that maybe this mage was the one that cursed him in the first place? How do you know he wasn't just using you?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: Of course it crossed our minds, but we didn't have a choice. The King was deteriorating by the hour.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: You could have gone to Lord Arceuus! You could have gone to Lord Shayzien! You could have gone to anyone apart from some random mage!

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: This mage. Have you met him since?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: Yes. Rose's condition...

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: You mean the condition you gave her?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: Her condition has no cure, but it can be kept in check with regular treatment. He meets with me and gives me the potions she needs.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: How do you know it's not the potions that are doing this to her?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: I've done my research. The potions are safe, and she can't live without them.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: Where is this mage?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: We meet outside Molch. I think he lives in the temple there, with the lizardmen.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: This mage. We need to find out who he is.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: I'll go to Molch. If he's there, I'll find him.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: Cutscene ends.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: Good luck out there. I'll keep an eye on this... I don't even have a word for him.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: Try not to kill him.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: I'll do my best.

options.text: How are you doing?

steps.player: How are you doing?

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: I'd rather not talk about it. We have work to focus on. There'll be plenty of time to contemplate later.

options.text: How are things back at the castle?

steps.player: How are things back at the castle?

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Terrible. I take it you heard about Martin?

steps.player: The arrest? I was there.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Such a stupid move. I told Councillor Andrews not to do it, but he listened to Lawry instead. Now the protestors are even angrier.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: At this rate, it's only a matter of time before things get violent. I even had Councillor Unkar moved to the castle for his own safety.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Not that he deserves safety! What a mess this is.

options.text: I'd better be off.

steps.player: I'd better be off.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: Councillor.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: Oh, hello there.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: I have a question for you.

options.text: What do you know of this mage?

steps.player: What do you know of this mage?

steps.speaker: Councillor Orson
steps.text: Very little. It was David... Sorry, Councillor Andrews, who he contacted first. The rest of us didn't meet him until much later.

steps.speaker: Councillor Orson
steps.text: He was an expert in old curses. He could see what was wrong with the King. He told Councillor Andrews and offered his help.

steps.speaker: Councillor Orson
steps.text: By then, it was already too late. The King had deteriorated too much. There was only one solution.

steps.player: I don't know if that's true.

steps.speaker: Councillor Orson
steps.text: You weren't there. You didn't see what was happening to him. There was no time to consider other options. We did what we had to do.

steps.player: If you say so. You said he lives in Molch?

steps.speaker: Councillor Orson
steps.text: That's right. In the temple, I think.

steps.player: A mysterious mage with no name who lives with some lizardmen. He sure sounds like an upstanding citizen with nothing suspicious about him at all.

steps.speaker: Councillor Orson
steps.text: You're not funny. Do you think we'd have worked with him if we knew all of that? We didn't find out about the lizardman connection until much later. By then, the deed had already been done.

steps.player: I'm suprised you'd even care about lizardman. They're pretty tame compared to demon summoning.

steps.speaker: Councillor Orson
steps.text: Sophia wasn't always like that. Before she joined that cult, she was just like the rest of us. The only difference was that she had other beliefs.

steps.player: Zamorakian beliefs aren't particularly welcome in most places.

steps.speaker: Councillor Orson
steps.text: So what? People should be entitled to their beliefs!

steps.player: Sure, but I suspect being entitled to summon demons is more up for debate.

steps.speaker: Councillor Orson
steps.text: Like I said, she wasn't always like that.

options.text: What happened with Rose?

steps.player: What happened with Rose?

steps.speaker: Councillor Orson
steps.text: I know you probably don't believe it, but we always meant for her to take the throne.

steps.player: I guess I'd probably have an easier time believing that if she wasn't lying right here instead.

steps.speaker: Councillor Orson
steps.text: She overheard us talking about the King. We couldn't let her tell anyone.

steps.player: But why? If it was really all about her, why would it matter what happened to you?

steps.speaker: Councillor Orson
steps.text: Because without us, who would have been left to rule? We had to do it for the good of Kourend.

steps.player: Did you? Or have you lied to yourself so much that you now actually believe it?

steps.speaker: Councillor Orson
steps.text: She was like a daughter to me!

steps.player: So you poisoned her?

steps.speaker: Councillor Orson
steps.text: And I have taken care of her every day since! Without me, she wouldn't even be alive.

steps.player: Is what she has now really much of a life at all?

steps.speaker: Councillor Orson
steps.text: You don't understand...

steps.player: To be honest, I don't know if I want to.

options.text: Actually, never mind.

steps.player: Actually, never mind.
