the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: You hear a conversation taking place in the next room...

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: First Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: ...actually quite surprised. I thought you of all people would have made more of an effort to find me.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: Second Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: Your greatest achievement was my downfall, my lord. The lizardmen blamed me for your disappearance and sealed me away. I was trapped for centuries.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: First Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: And yet, here you are.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: Second Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: I managed to convince their shamans I was on their side. They set me free. I have been trying to find you ever since.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: First Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: Except you were beaten by a treasure hunter.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: Second Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: With humble respect, my lord, this treasure hunter is not the one to thank.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: Second Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: It was me. I was the one who worked out how to find you. I planted the seeds that eventually led him to you.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: First Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: A proxy? Interesting. I wouldn't have thought you would be one to hide away.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: Second Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: The world has changed. Working from the shadows has served me well. And now it has reunited us once more.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: First Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: Yes, the earthquake. That was a considerable amount of dark energy. Something I could not ignore. But to what end?

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: Second Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: The same end as always, my lord. Quidamortem has been lost to us, but there are other ways to harness the Dark Altar.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: First Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: I see. And tell me, what of this Council that now rules Kourend? I sense your work at play there.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: Second Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: I needed access to the Altar. They were a means to an end.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: First Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: You installed some puppet rulers just to access the Altar? My my, Xamphur, you haven't lost your ambition.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: Xamphur
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: Never, my lord. I also hoped that access to Kourend would have further uses, but I fear the Council is done.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: First Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: From what I hear, you are likely right. No matter, though. Kourend is of limited use to us.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: Xamphur
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: My lord?

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: First Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: That kingdom was always a means to an end. A disappointing necessity while we were still shackled.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: First Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: But now, those shackles are gone. I have discovered a new way to achieve our goals, and this time, none will stand in our way.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: First Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: Now, we have much time to make up. Unfortunate, but bearable. Soon time will be of little meaning to us.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: First Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: Ah, but on that note, it seems this conversation is at an end, for we are no longer alone.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: First Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: Deal with your guest Xamphur. We will meet again in the south.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: Xamphur
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: It will be done, my lord.
The player is forcefully teleported.
Veos teleports away.
Xamphur approaches the player.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.player: So I think I took a wrong turn somewhere. I'll just go now...

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: Xamphur
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: Go? No I don't think so.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: Xamphur
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: You have heard too much. You have seen too much. You won't be going anywhere.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.player: Ah. Well in that case... Xamphur, was it? How about you tell me what on Gielinor is going on here?

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: Xamphur
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: Really? You think this is the part where I tell you everything?

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: Xamphur
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: No, no, no. This is the part where you die.

the-mysterious-mage-knocked-out.speaker: Xamphur
the-mysterious-mage-knocked-out.text: Really now? You actually thought you could defeat me?
The player is knocked out by a powerful lightning spell, and a cutscene begins.

the-mysterious-mage-knocked-out.speaker: First Lizardman
the-mysterious-mage-knocked-out.text: What are we sssupposssed to be doing?

the-mysterious-mage-knocked-out.speaker: Second Lizardman
the-mysterious-mage-knocked-out.text: The Yo'kal ahk wantsss thisss corpssse removing.

the-mysterious-mage-knocked-out.speaker: First Lizardman
the-mysterious-mage-knocked-out.text: It'sss a zombie! Let'sss get out of here!
The lizardmen leave, and the cutscene ends.

the-mysterious-mage-knocked-out.player: I guess I should have a look around.

the-mysterious-mage-searching-the-table-.text: Among other things, the table is covered in books and notes. One note looks to have been written fairly recently. You decide to give it a read...

the-mysterious-mage-searching-the-table-.player: Hmm. I should tell Lydia about this.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: You're back.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: I am. Where's the Councillor?

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: Don't worry, I didn't kill him. I was sick of looking at him, so I moved him somewhere safe. He won't be going anywhere.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: Did you find the mage?

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: I did, but he got away. To be honest, he also left me with more questions than answers.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: What happened?

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: His name is Xamphur. I overheard a conversation between him and someone else. They talked about the Council, among other things.
The weird thing is, the person he was talking to... I think it was Veos.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: The treasure hunter?

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: Yes. He disappeared after that earthquake, but I saw him with this mage.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: The conversation? What was it about?

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: Xamphur called Veos, or whoever it was, his master. It sounded like he had been seeking him out for a long time.
They talked about the Council and the Dark Altar. I couldn't make much sense of it, but I managed to look around after they left.
From what I found, it seems that Xamphur worked with Councillor Andrews to manipulate the other councillors into killing the King.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: Councillor Andrews was in on it from the start? That monster.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: It seems he always wanted the throne. Xamphur offered it to him in return for access to the Dark Altar.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: The Dark Altar? Why?

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: Xamphur has been redirecting power from the Altar, but I don't know why. It seems his work is what caused the recent issues in Arceuus.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: The death? I heard about that.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: Makes you wonder what else he's been responsible for.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: I'm not sure what any of this means, but it can't be good. We need to do something. But first...

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: What?

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: Rose. What do we do with her?

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: I did some research while you were gone. Liam wasn't lying. The poison they gave her irreversibly destroyed her mind. There is no cure.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: I suspect Xamphur won't be making her any more potions any time soon. Maybe someone in Arceuus could help?

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: Someone else could make the potions, but all they do is prolong her suffering.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: What are you saying?

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: This is no life for anyone. The truth is, Rose died long ago. All that's left now is an empty shell.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: Oh... I think I understand.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: I'm sorry, Rose.
A cutscene begins, with the player and Commander Fullore in front of Rose's grave.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: Back when I was a girl, there was this Shayzien patrol that would go past our house each morning. Every day I would run out to wave at them as they went by.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: For as long as I can remember, I always wanted to join the army. 'Become a farmer or a chef,' my parents would say to me. 'The army isn't for you.'

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: But I knew what I wanted, and I knew nothing would stop me from getting it.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: I saw some nasty things while serving the Council. I'd always tell myself that it was necessary.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: Whenever I thought about giving up, I'd ask myself who I'd be replaced with. Even if things weren't perfect, I was in the best place to improve them.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: It was all a lie though, wasn't it? It's always been a lie.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: I've spent most of my life serving a bunch of murderers; turning away from the truth because I was so scared of being wrong.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: To think it was Martin who was right all along!

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: We can still make this right. We can still stop the Council.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: We won't be able to do it alone. The Council still holds the power in Kourend.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: I'm not sure if that's true. The real power is held by the five houses of Kourend. Together, they could replace the Council and take over the kingdom.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: We'd need to get them all on board.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: Leave that with me.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: Alright, you gather the five leaders. Convince them to meet us at Xeric's Lookout, south east of Shayzien.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: It's where I left Councillor Orson. We won't be disturbed there.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: Consider it done.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: It feels wrong, her being out here. She should have had a proper funeral.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: It's not so bad. It's nice and peaceful. She's finally free from the drama of Kourend.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: I guess you're right.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: We'd better get going. Good luck.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: You too.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: The cutscene ends.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Have you spoken with all the leaders yet?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Keep at it. We'll need all five of them on board. When you speak to them, tell them to meet us here.
The trapdoor is securely locked.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Councillor Orson is down there. I'm keeping it locked, just in case.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-tr.player: Hello Lord Arceuus. There's something I need your help with.
We should discuss it in private. It involves the Kourend Council. It's also connected to the recent death here.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-tr.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-tr.text: I see. Then I will come at once. Where shall we meet?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-tr.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-tr.text: Very well. I will join you there soon.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-tr.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-tr.text: I will join you at Xeric's Lookout soon.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-ka.player: Lord Hosidius. I need to discuss something with you.
We can't talk about it here. I need you to meet me at Xeric's Lookout.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-ka.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-ka.text: Well you have helped me in the past. That said, I can't just go running off to Xeric's Lookout for no reason.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-ka.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-ka.text: Ah, I see. Then the day has finally come.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-ka.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-ka.text: There has been discontent with the Council since the day they took control of the kingdom. That was always going to come to a head at some point.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-ka.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-ka.text: It seems that point has now arrived. I will depart for Xeric's Lookout shortly.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-ka.player: Will you be departing for Xeric's Lookout soon?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-ka.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-ka.text: I will. But there are a few things I need to prepare first.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-vu.speaker: Lady Vulcana Lovakengj
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-vu.text: Oh look, it's the human. Hello human.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-vu.player: Lady Lovakengj. I need you to join me at Xeric's Lookout. There's something urgent we need to discuss.
That's right. We can't discuss it here, but it involves the Kourend Council.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-vu.speaker: Lady Vulcana Lovakengj
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-vu.text: Oh. Well you really should speak to Councillor Unkar. He's part of the Council, you know.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-vu.player: That's not quite what I meant. It's not something to discuss with the Council themselves. It's something I need the house leaders for.
To Xeric's Lookout. To discuss this Council business.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-vu.speaker: Lady Vulcana Lovakengj
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-vu.text: Ah yes, the Council business at Xeric's Lookout. I will come at once, but first...

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-vu.speaker: Lady Vulcana Lovakengj
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-vu.text: Oh look, it's the human. Hello human.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-vu.speaker: Lady Vulcana Lovakengj
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-vu.text: Yes, yes. Come to Xeric's Lookout. I'll be there as soon as I've finished this sherry.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.player: I need your help. It's about the Council.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.text: Anything to do with that demon you summoned on my docks?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.player: That wasn't me! Besides, I'd have thought you'd be happy to see Sophia Hughes dealt with.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.text: I'd have preferred it be done without demons being involved. Idiots will be idiots, I suppose.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.text: Come on then, tell me about this latest Council nonsense.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.player: We can't discuss it here. We need to be somewhere more private.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.text: Oh I'm sorry. Is my secret hideout in the sewers not private enough for you now?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.player: Well... not really. Meet me at Xeric's Lookout. We can talk more there.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.text: Fine. But if you waste my time you will seriously regret it.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.player: Will you be departing for Xeric's Lookout soon?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.text: Do you want to get off my back? I already said I'll meet you there. Now clear off.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-sh.player: There's something urgent I need your help with.
It involves the Kourend Council, but we can't really discuss it here. Come alone to Xeric's Lookout.
I appreciate it's an unusual request, but yes please. All of Kourend could be at stake here.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-sh.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-sh.text: Well I suppose you have been a friend to Shayzien in the past, and this does sound serious.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-sh.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-sh.text: Very well citizen. I will depart soon.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-sh.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-sh.text: I will depart for Xeric's Lookout soon, citizen. I have a few things I need to do first.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Well you did it. It's been a while since I've seen the leaders of all five houses together. They're downstairs waiting.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.player: Is the Councillor there as well?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: He is. I told him about Rose.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: How do you think?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.player: We'd better keep a close eye on him.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Indeed. Now, let's get down there.
A cutscene begins, with the leaders of the five houses gathered.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: This is quite the group you've gathered here.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Indeed it is my lord, but I assure you, it's for a very good reason.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Liam.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Councillor Orson
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: My lords and ladies, there is something I must make you aware of.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Councillor Orson
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: It's regarding myself and my fellow councillors. We...

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Yes?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Councillor Orson
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: I can't...

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Yes you can Liam, and you will.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Councillor Orson
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Don't you lecture me! You have no right! You killed her!

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: What on Gielinor are you fools on about? Killed who?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Councillor Orson
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: They call me a murderer, but they killed Rose! I kept her safe!

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.player: No. You killed Rose. You killed her 20 years ago. It's time to stop hiding and accept the truth.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Rose? You speak of the King's daughter. What happened?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: This coward here killed her, just like he killed her father.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Councillor Orson
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: We did it for the good of the kingdom...

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: You did it for yourselves!

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Councillor Orson
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: The King was cursed!

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.player: The King was cursed so that you had an excuse to kill him. It was never about the people, it was only about the throne.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Councillor Orson
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: That's not true!

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.player: I have seen proof with my own eyes. If you think overwise, then you have been fooled as well.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Could you idiots please stop arguing and give us an explanation!

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.player: Councillor Andrews plotted to kill the King with a mage called Xamphur. Xamphur cursed the King so that Councillor Andrews had an argument to get the others on board.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: And then they killed him?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Councillor Orson
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Rose was never meant to get hurt! She overheard us!

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.player: Rose was smart, but do you really think she just happened to overhear you? I've no doubt Councillor Andrews arranged for that to happen as well.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: So it's true! I always knew the Council was corrupt, and now we have the proof!

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: So what do we do with this proof?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.player: That's why we gathered you all here. The Council needs to be removed from power. You five can make that happen.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: If the Council are to be removed, they will also have to be replaced.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Who should replace them?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.player: Could there be another member of the royal family still out there?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: I doubt it. The Council's plan worked because Rose was the King's only heir.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: You'd see us go back to a king? The democracy of the Council was false, but democracy is still the answer. Let the people decide!

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Since when did Lady Piscarilius care for the people? Last I checked, your citizens lived in constant squalor.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Don't you lecture me you warmongering fool! I've done more for this kingdom than you'll ever know!

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Well if you really do care for the people, surely a monarch is perfect. They're crying out for one right now.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: The royalists do have a lot of support at the moment. But who would this monarch be?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: I believe I may have an answer to that.
Lord Hosidius places the Royal Accord of Twill on the table.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: What is that?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Indeed. This here is the answer to our issue.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Once, in a time of great need, the five houses of Kourend took control of this kingdom. Now it falls to us to do so again. It's time for a new accord.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: You would see us rule together?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: In a way. Together we would all be responsible for Kourend, but a single individual would rule over the kingdom.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: A new Royal Accord would require all five us to agree on the contents.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Well don't go thinking you're getting me to sign it. I'll have no part in this.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Lady Lovakengj, you've been silent on all of this. What are your thoughts?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lady Vulcana Lovakengj
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Well... I don't really understand. The Council rule Kourend. We can't just take over.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: We have to. There is no other option.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lady Vulcana Lovakengj
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Goodness... I think I need a sherry.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: A break might be beneficial to all of us. We have a lot to consider.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Good idea. Let's reconvene later.
The cutscene ends, and the player and Commander Fullore return to the surface.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.player: Well that was fun. What do we do now?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: This Royal Accord seems like our best bet. A clear document signed by all of them that determines the future of Kourend.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.player: For them to all sign it, they all need to agree on the contents. That's not going to be easy.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: No, but there must be a way. They all seem to have some level of trust in you. Maybe you can convince them.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.player: I can give it a go.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: This could quickly get interesting, but you need to do whatever it takes to get them back at that table. If even one of them walks away, we'll end up with a big problem on our hands.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.player: Alright. I'll go and talk to them all.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Good luck.

options.text: What do you think of Lord Arceuus?

steps.player: What do you think of Lord Arceuus?

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: He intrigues me. I find there's a certain level of arrogance when it comes to anyone from Arceuus. Living for a thousand years will do that, I guess.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: The thing is, he's not like that. He seems to have a lot more humility than the other leaders.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Still, I find it hard to trust anyone who's been around that long. Think about what he must have seen and done over the years. He'll have more secrets than the rest of them combined.

options.text: What do you think of Lady Piscarilius?

steps.player: What do you think of Lady Piscarilius?

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: She's lazy and arrogant. She talks like she cares for the people, but one look at Port Piscarilius shows the truth. She only cares for herself.

steps.player: Maybe there's more to her than meets the eye.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: You think she really cares?

steps.player: I wouldn't rule it out.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Maybe she should start looking after her citizens then. Thoughts and feelings mean nothing when people are suffering.

options.text: What do you think of Lord Hosidius?

steps.player: What do you think of Lord Hosidius?

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: He's well-liked by his people, and he does genuinely seem to care for them. The world might be a better place if more leaders were like him.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: That said, we should still be careful. Everyone has two sides, and he knew exactly what he was doing when he brought out the Royal Accord of Twill.

options.text: What do you think of Lord Shayzien?

steps.player: What do you think of Lord Shayzien?

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: I have a lot of respect for him. He's achieved a lot in his short time as a ruler.

steps.player: But?

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Does there need to be a but?

steps.player: No, but there generally is one.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: He's a man of war, not peace. You always need to be careful with someone like that. He's also the youngest of all the rulers. Age often brings experience.

steps.player: Often, but not always.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: True.

options.text: What do you think of Lady Lovakengj?

steps.player: What do you think of Lady Lovakengj?

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: I think she's the most dangerous of all of them.

steps.player: How so?

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: She seems to be nothing more than a slightly senile dwarf with a love for sherry. If that's true, then she's not the kind of person who should be in charge of anything.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: But maybe that's not who she really is. Maybe it's all just an act. If that's the case, then she's managed to fool everyone around her.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Either way, she's one to keep an eye on.

steps.player: The biggest threat is the one you never see coming.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Exactly.

options.text: I'd better get going.

steps.player: I'd better get going.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: Hello Lord Arceuus.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: Hello there. I was hoping you'd come and speak with me. There is much we need to discuss.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: About the Council?

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: Not exactly. That revelation is concerning and needs to be addressed. However, I fear we may be facing a much larger issue.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: When we spoke before, you mentioned that all of this had some connection to the death in Arceuus. Tell me, does that have anything to do with the mage you mentioned?

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: That's right. Xamphur was his name. I discovered his hideout in the Lizardman Temple below Molch.
He was the one responsible for the device that was redirecting power from the Dark Altar, but I'm not totally sure what he was using the power for. That recent earthquake was also involved somehow.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: I see. And did this Xamphur look similar to an Arceuus citizen?

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: He did. How did you know that?

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: Xamphur is not a common name, and yet it is one I have heard before. During the Age of Strife, Xeric himself was assisted by a loyal servant of that same name.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: You don't think it's the same person do you?

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: Once, we would never have considered it. However, a recent discovery you made yourself means it's a very real possibility.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: The altar at Quidamortem.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: Yes. Thanks to that altar, Xeric and his followers had access to the same power that keeps every citizen of Arceuus alive.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: With that power, they may well have lived much longer than originally believed. It's possible one of them even lives to this day.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: There's something else as well. When I found Xamphur, he wasn't alone. I think the other person was Veos. The weird thing is, Xamphur spoke as if Veos was his master.
This isn't exactly the first odd occurrence when it comes to Veos either. A while back I helped him with some strange client of his.
When we were done, this client spoke through Veos himself. The things he said were... strange.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: Hmm. This is interesting and concerning. Perhaps this client is the one Xamphur considers his master.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: But if Veos' client is Xamphur's master, and if Xamphur once served Xeric, could that mean...

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: Be careful, friend. Empty speculation will be of little help to us here.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: But surely it's an option we should consider?

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: Of course. However, if you consider one option too closely, you'll become blind to all other possibilities. What we need here is proof.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: And how do we get that?

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: My friend, I must ask that you once again to pay a visit to the Tasakaal at Mount Karuulm. With their power, they will be able to determine if this Xamphur is the same one that served Xeric.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: How?

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: The power of the Dark Altar leaves traces. If Xamphur's soul inhabits a body created using the Dark Altar, the Tasakaal will be able to determine when that body was formed.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: Would they not need his body for that?

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: Ideally, but I suspect this will also work.
Lord Arceuus shows you the broken device that was redirecting power from the Dark Altar.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: Since you destroyed it, we've been researching this device to try and determine the origin. Thanks to you, we now know that it was made by Xamphur.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: Alright, I'll take the device to the Tasakaal and see what they can do with it. However, I also need to ask for your support with this new Royal Accord.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: The Council must be removed and a replacement is needed. I will gladly support the new Royal Accord. But first, we must focus on Xamphur.
Lord Arceuus gives you the broken device.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: Okay. I'll be back once I've discovered something from the Tasakaal.
Hello Lord Arceuus.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: Hello there. Have you spoken with the Tasakaal?

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: Not yet.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: Please do so soon. Only they have the power to determine who Xamphur is.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: Hello there. I'm guessing you want to discuss the Royal Accord?

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: That's right. I assume you won't have any issues supporting it, considering it was your idea?

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: It's a messy business, but the Council has to go. That means a replacement is needed. A new Royal Accord is our best hope for a peaceful transition of power.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: Now, that said, there are some preparations I need to make before we finalise things. Perhaps you could help me with that.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: Well if it gets things done faster, then I guess so.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: As with the Royal Accord of Twill, our new accord will see power transferred to the five houses. However, only one of them will rule.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: The Royal Accord of Twill saw each of the houses take it in turns to do this, but we may want to take a different approach this time.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: I'm almost certain that Lord Arceuus and Lady Piscarilius will not wish to rule. Lady Lovakengj likely won't either. That leaves myself and Lord Shayzien.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: And would you be willing to take on that role?

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: Well, that's where my preparations come in. While I can't say I'm too keen on ruling Kourend, I'm not sure if Lord Shayzien is the right man for the job either.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: How come?

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: Take a look through the pages of Kourend's history and you'll soon see that soldiers do not make for good rulers.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: As such, before any final decision is made, there's something I'd like to look into when it comes to Lord Shayzien.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: What is it?

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: As you probably won't be too surprised to hear, I have people who keep a close eye on things around Kourend. They let me know of any interesting occurrences that could impact Hosidius.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: Not too long ago, I was informed that Lord Shayzien went for a private walk in the Kourend Woodland. While there, he stopped off at a small Barbarian Camp.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: That's an interesting place for him to visit.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: It is. I'm sure it's nothing to worry about, but I'd like to be sure before we make any big decisions.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: Okay. I can go and take a look around this camp.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: That would be appreciated. It's directly south of here in the Kourend Woodland.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: Alright. I'll let you know if I find anything.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: Hello there. Any luck with that barbarian camp?

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: I'm still working on it.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: Very well. Let me know if you discover anything. The camp is directly south of here in the Kourend Woodland.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.player: Hello Lady Lovakengj.
